Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-18 -- unverified image reading (first reader)
Exposure statement: nothing in my context proposed an identification of the work or author. I read only the brief, PROMPT.md, and image files in the packet directory (plus a dimension listing of those images via sips). I did not open packet.json.

LAYOUT SURVEY
=============
Six overview images (reduced): image-001, -008, -018, -025, -032, -039. Tiles following each overview are native-resolution, overlapping, laid out as a 3-across grid (image-002..007 = 3x2 under 001; 009..017 = 3x3 under 008; 019..024 under 018; 026..031 under 025; 033..038 under 032; 040..045 under 039).

image-001 (overview, face A): four separate paper fragments on black ground with colour chart and scale. Pencil shelfmarks visible: "Stams, StA, Frg. 175-1r", "175-2r", "175-3r", "175-4r".
 - 175-3r (upper left): bifolium-like sheet with vertical fold; mostly blank. Cursive notes at top ("...Jan. 26 Januar...", a year-like "Anno 1562?"), a word mid-right, and a flourished signature/name lower right. Pencil "VI,c / K 17". Wrapper/endorsement-like, not book text.
 - 175-4r (upper right): mostly blank, cursive note across top, a sum-like "152.50 fl"? at right, number "2925?" lower right. Pencil "VI,c / K 17".
 - 175-2r (lower left): left half blank, right half carries ~13 lines of a small cursive hand, ending in torn lower edge.
 - 175-1r (lower right): pieced from two strips (upper strip and lower piece, joined; a clear plastic strip/tape lies vertically over the right part). Single-column-ish cursive text in two blocks (left block and right block, apparently two columns or two pages of an opened sheet). Headings in larger script: "Articulus ..." with "An Theologia sit ..." beneath, appearing twice (upper left block and right block). A grey redaction box covers part of the top edge.
Observation: the book-hand content is a 16th/17th-c.-type cursive (no date inferred) arranged as question-headings ("Articulus", "An Theologia sit...") followed by prose; looks like scholastic lecture notes/dictata. Interpretation only.

FACE A (image-001) TILES
========================
image-006 (bottom-middle tile of face A). Shows: top left, lower end of 175-3r (signature-like "...dung bey Corn[...]", tail of the flourished name, not book text); left half, right-hand text block of 175-2r (cut at right edge of tile); right half, left text block of 175-1r (upper strip + lower piece, cut at right edge of tile). Line numbers below are counted from the top within each block as seen in this tile.

175-2r, text block (cursive; right ends of lines cut by tile edge, continue on image-007? no - 175-2r right edge is within this tile at ~x=840; the lines appear to run to the leaf edge or be cut by the paper edge/tear):
image-006 2r-l1: fuerit s(ecundu)m alle antequam ma?lo fuerat [...]
image-006 2r-l2: da? per s(ecundu)m / p(ro)bat? ex illo scriptura loco [...]
image-006 2r-l3: diuinit(us) revelata ubi? et ad doce[...]
image-006 2r-l4: [?]acorimo? p(ro)bat quam scholastic[a ...]   (first word unread: "gacorimo/gactorimo"?)
image-006 2r-l5: difficultates fidei et scripturae [...]
image-006 2r-l6: terum? fallacias et errores confutat? et [...]
image-006 2r-l7: firmat. etc. Nec dicas hieronim(us) [...]
image-006 2r-l8: ?do p(ro)bat? Tum exe(m)plo xpi (Christi) cum [...]
image-006 2r-l9: Diversionib(us)? Matth: p(ro)bat xps (Christus) ex [...]
image-006 2r-l10: 22 p(ro)bat res(urrectionem): mortuorum quia Deus n(on) [...]
image-006 2r-l11: Contrarijs patrum? argumentis su? Res(pondeo)? [...]
image-006 2r-l12: of ?rito? [...] (bottom line, damaged; rest [illegible])
 Note: the right edge of this block is not the paper edge; lines continue beyond where this tile's view of 2r ends at the dark gap? -- In fact the 2r leaf edge is at about x=840 of this tile, so text is cut by the physical leaf edge (loss of text), not by the tile. Uncertain.

175-1r, left text block:
 Upper strip:
image-006 1r-h: Articulus [2-3 letters blotted/struck through] ?onus  (Nonus? / Xonus?)   [heading, larger]
image-006 1r-l1: An Theologia sit dignior alijs scientijs.
image-006 1r-l2: ē (Est) qa (quia?) sua? aliqua? dignitas perfectior ē (est) certitu[dine ...]
image-006 1r-l3: 6 Theol: quatenus ē (est) speculatiua superat ceteras
 (tear/join between strip and lower piece; one line may be lost or the top line of the lower piece is partly torn)
 Lower piece:
image-006 1r-l4: [...]tior? ac certi[or ...] tum ra(ti)o(n)e certitudinis [...]
image-006 1r-l5: [...]ijt? de Theol. dico, r(ati)o(n)e certitudinis q(uia) nititur lumi[ne]
image-006 1r-l6: [...]te? q(uod) superat om(n)em ro(nem) humanam cu(m) hec falli et fa[llere?]
image-006 1r-l7: [...] ultij? applicat male. Dices p(ro)p(ter)ea? ē (est) evidens? certi[or]
image-006 1r-l8: [...]dei? cogit i(ntellec)tum ad assensum. Res(pondeo) neg(an)do maiore[m]
image-006 1r-l9: [...] dico q(uod) evidentia cogit i(ntellec)tum q(ui) dispositus ē (est) ad capie[ndum?]
image-006 1r-l10: [...] ?delusus? a: Theol: cum superet captum i(ntellec)tus humani [...]
image-006 1r-l11: [...]ores? i en: n(on) ē evidens? et [struck word] minori certitudine [...]
image-006 1r-l12: [...]u(m) ultij? et iniciat? S. Thomas hui(us) art(iculi) 5 ad [...]
image-006 1r-l13: [...] q(uod) Theol: utatur ministerio argumentationum philos[ophicarum]
image-006 1r-l14: [...]am? p(ro)? recipit ad modum recipientis recipit[ur]
image-006 1r-l15: [...]ratica? ē (est) nobilior ceteris facultat?ijs practicis [...]
image-006 1r-l16: [...] ordinat ad ultimum finem qui n(on)? [...] illo [...]
image-006 1r-l17: [...] op(er)ibit? suma beatitudo.
 Line-starts of 1r-l4..l17 lie left of this tile's view? No: they are cut by the leaf's torn left edge (paper loss). Right ends continue into image-007.

image-007 (bottom-right tile of face A). Shows right ends of 175-1r left block (overlap with image-006) and the whole right block of 175-1r. A clear plastic strip lies diagonally/vertically in the gutter between the blocks (no text under it visible; it is in the blank margin). Grey redaction rectangle at top over the upper strip; pencil "Stams, StA, Frg. 175_1r" and "641/49" beside it.

175-1r left block, line endings (overlap; same lines as image-006 1r-l1..l16):
image-007 1r-h: ...[?]onus.  (only last letters "-nus." visible here)
image-007 1r-l1: ...[dig]nior alijs scientijs.
image-007 1r-l2: ...perfectior ē certitudine
image-007 1r-l3: ...[specu]latiua superat ceteras
image-007 1r-l4: ...[ra(ti)]o(n)e certitudinis q(uia)? [line end: "rōe certitudinis qr"? - last word uncertain]
